item.title: Mathpocalypse ruins crypto forever — 16 replies — 3.9/hr
item.content:encoded:
Mathpocalypse ruins crypto forever

Open thread • Replies: 16 • Updated: 2026-10-10 10:36 UTC

OP

So OAI oneshots 20% of outstanding math problems. Nerds on xitter call for imminent breach of ecdsa cryptography which, by extension, means all coins (or at least, all the coins that matter) break. This is clearly bullshit and highly unlikely. And yet, this still ruins all coins, forever. It doesn't matter that this specific breakthrough didn't destroy cryptography. All that matters is that AI is now producing, at some rate, mathematical miracles that teams of humans working on the same problems for decades on end never could. AI today is the worst it will ever be, so that means whatever the rate of miracles it produces today is, that rate will only increase as time goes on. Nobody can prove that AI has or will break modern cryptography, but nobody can prove that it won't, either. Meanwhile the miracles keep coming, faster and faster. If you're holding the bag when the wrong miracle happens, it goes to zero overnight. Everyone perceives this new state of affairs and sees that there is no expiration date on it, and elects to sell before other people sell because in this new state of affairs you can either sell now, sell later for less, or hold until cryptography breaks and your bags go to zero.

Again, this is all bullshit. Nobody's going to break ecdsa or public key cryptography. And if they did, they wouldn't blow their cover by draining a crypto wallet. And if they did, they would never bother targeting your wallet. And none of this matters, because crypto is a beauty contest where the only thing that matters is guessing what other people are thinking and then acting on that information before they do. This is not like quantum where qday is approaching, but we can measure its approach and take appropriate measures ahead of time. This is a situation where the break might already be here, and by the time you can know it is it's already too late. So the only sane thing to do is sell now before you can't sell at all.

Open thread • Replies: 68 • Updated: 2026-10-10 08:25 UTC

OP

Today, my friend was talking to a group of people at the gym.

He started listing economic statistics and asking why everyone was at the gym instead of working. They explained that their classes were finished for the day or that they had the day off.

My friend told the students that if they were still in school, they should definitely be working, because the economy is terrible and they probably don’t want to wake up at 30 and realize they’re working full-time. He told the other that if they were available to hang out at the gym during the day, that probably meant they didn’t have some high-paying white-collar 9-to-5 job and were likely just making wages.

One guy asked him, “Why are you telling people they have no future?”

My friend responded that he wasn’t telling anyone they had no future. He was merely presenting economic data and statistics.

Then the guy said something along the lines of, “People today are living a lot better than someone 50 years ago.”

My friend argued that people working back then were actually working toward a great future. The guy responded, “People have always had to work. People today are working toward a future too.”

“No. People working today are getting royally screwed. There has been basically zero wage growth since 2020 while rich people have doubled their money. Meanwhile, everything is getting more expensive.”

The guy responded, “Yeah, well, not everyone has the opportunity to get rich.”

My friend said that since the end of World War II, there have essentially been endless opportunities for every family to make money and build wealth. If someone isn’t successful today, maybe their family is simply low IQ.

Was my friend completely out of his mind, or is there actually something to his argument?

Are people today genuinely getting screwed economically, or are we just romanticizing the past?
